      print '(A,I4,A,I2)', 'Iteration ', i, ' executed by thread ', thread_id
      !$omp end critical
    end if
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do

end program demo_omp_parallel_do

ompdosimd.title: omp_parallel_do_simd
ompdosimd.name: omp_parallel_do_simd

params.private(list): Creates thread-private copies of listed variables. Within each thread, SIMD lanes may share or privatize these variables depending on the implementation.
params.shared(list): Specifies variables shared among all threads. Arrays accessed with the loop index are typically shared.
params.reduction(operator:list): Performs a reduction operation. The implementation combines both thread-level and SIMD-level reductions efficiently. Operators: +, -, *, .and., .or., .eqv., .neqv., max, min, iand, ior, ieor.
params.simdlen(length): Specifies the preferred number of SIMD lanes. Should match the hardware vector width for best performance (e.g., 4 for SSE with double, 8 for AVX with single).
params.safelen(length): Maximum number of iterations that can be executed concurrently without violating dependencies. If there are no loop-carried dependencies, this can be omitted.
params.aligned(list:alignment): Declares that array addresses are aligned to the specified byte boundary. Enables aligned vector load/store instructions. Common values: 16 (SSE), 32 (AVX), 64 (AVX-512).
params.linear(list:step): Specifies that listed variables have a linear relationship with the loop iteration, incrementing by step each iteration.
params.collapse(n): Combines n nested loops into a single iteration space before distributing and vectorizing.

ompdosimd.description:
**!$omp parallel do simd** creates a parallel region containing a combined worksharing-loop and SIMD construct. Loop iterations are first distributed across threads, then each thread's iterations are vectorized using SIMD instructions. This provides two levels of parallelism: thread-level parallelism from the parallel do and data-level parallelism from SIMD vectorization.

 The loop body must be suitable for vectorization: no function calls (unless declared as simd), no I/O operations, no dependencies between SIMD lanes beyond what safelen allows, and operations should be uniform or linear.
ompdosimd.result: The parallel do simd construct achieves both thread-level parallelism and SIMD vectorization. Loop iterations are distributed across threads, and each thread processes its iterations using vector instructions. Upon completion, any reduction variables contain the fully combined result from all threads and all SIMD lanes.
ompdosimd.example_code:
program demo_omp_parallel_do_simd
  use omp_lib
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n = 10000
  real(8), allocatable :: a(:), b(:), c(:)
  real(8) :: sum_val, dot_product_val
  integer :: i

  allocate(a(n), b(n), c(n))

  ! Initialize arrays
  do i = 1, n
    a(i) = real(i, 8) * 0.001d0
    b(i) = real(n - i + 1, 8) * 0.001d0
  end do

  ! Parallel do simd: array addition with SIMD vectorization
  !$omp parallel do simd private(i) shared(a, b, c) simdlen(8)
  do i = 1, n
    c(i) = a(i) + b(i)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do simd

  print '(A,F12.6)', 'c(1)   = ', c(1)
  print '(A,F12.6)', 'c(n)   = ', c(n)
  print '(A,F12.6)', 'c(n/2) = ', c(n/2)

  ! Parallel do simd with reduction: sum
  sum_val = 0.0d0
  !$omp parallel do simd private(i) reduction(+:sum_val)
  do i = 1, n
    sum_val = sum_val + c(i)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do simd

  print '(A,F15.6)', 'Sum of c: ', sum_val

  ! Parallel do simd: dot product
  dot_product_val = 0.0d0
  !$omp parallel do simd private(i) reduction(+:dot_product_val)
  do i = 1, n
    dot_product_val = dot_product_val + a(i) * b(i)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do simd

  print '(A,F15.6)', 'Dot product a.b: ', dot_product_val

  deallocate(a, b, c)

end program demo_omp_parallel_do_simd

ompparallel.title: omp_parallel
ompparallel.name: omp parallel
ompparallel.summary: Creates a team of threads to execute a parallel region

params.private(list): Creates a new instance of each listed variable for each thread. The initial value is undefined. Variables must be definable.
params.shared(list): Specifies that listed variables are shared among all threads in the team. All threads access the same storage location.
params.default(none|shared|private|firstprivate: Sets the default data-sharing attribute for variables referenced in the parallel region. Using `none` requires explicit specification of all variables. Only one DEFAULT clause is allowed per directive.
params.firstprivate(list): Like private, but each thread's copy is initialized from the original variable's value before the parallel region.
params.copyin(list): Copies the master thread's THREADPRIVATE common block data to the thread-private copies at the start of the parallel region.
params.reduction([modifier,]operator:list): Performs a reduction operation. Each thread has a private copy initialized appropriately. At region end, values are combined using the specified operator (+, *, -, .and., .or., .eqv., .neqv., max, min, iand, ior, ieor).
params.if([parallel:]scalar-logical-expression): If the expression evaluates to .false., the region executes serially with a single thread.
params.num_threads(scalar-integer-expression): Specifies the number of threads in the team. Must evaluate to a positive integer. Overrides OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable.
params.proc_bind(master|close|spread): Specifies the mapping of threads to places. `master` binds threads to the master's place, `close` binds to places close to the master, `spread` distributes threads across available places.
params.allocate([allocator:]list): Specifies the memory allocator for private variables.

ompparallel.description:
**!$omp parallel** creates a team of threads that execute the enclosed
 structured block in parallel. When a thread encounters a parallel construct,
 a team of threads is created. The thread that encountered the construct
 becomes the master thread (thread number 0) of the new team. All threads
 in the team, including the master thread, execute the parallel region.
 Once the team is created, the number of threads remains constant for
 the duration of that parallel region. At the end of the parallel region,
 an implicit barrier synchronizes all threads before only the master
 thread continues execution.
ompparallel.result: The parallel construct creates a team of threads that execute the structured block concurrently. Upon completion of the parallel region, all threads synchronize at an implicit barrier, ensuring all parallel work is complete. Only the master thread (thread 0) continues execution after the parallel region. Any reduction variables contain the combined result from all threads. Private variables go out of scope at the end of the region.
ompparallel.example_code:
program demo_omp_parallel
  use omp_lib
  implicit none
  integer :: thread_id, num_threads
  integer :: i, n
  real :: sum_val, local_sum
  real, allocatable :: array(:)

  n = 1000
  allocate(array(n))
  array = [(real(i), i=1,n)]
  sum_val = 0.0

  ! Basic parallel region
  !$omp parallel private(thread_id) shared(num_threads)
    thread_id = omp_get_thread_num()
    if (thread_id == 0) then
      num_threads = omp_get_num_threads()
      print *, 'Number of threads:', num_threads
    end if
    print *, 'Hello from thread', thread_id
  !$omp end parallel

  ! Parallel region with reduction
  !$omp parallel default(none) shared(array, n) &
  !$omp& private(i, local_sum) reduction(+:sum_val)
    local_sum = 0.0
    !$omp do
    do i = 1, n
      local_sum = local_sum + array(i)
    end do
    !$omp end do
    sum_val = sum_val + local_sum
  !$omp end parallel

  print *, 'Sum of array:', sum_val

  ! Parallel region with conditional execution
  !$omp parallel if(n > 100) num_threads(4)
    print *, 'Executing with specified thread count'
  !$omp end parallel

  deallocate(array)
end program demo_omp_parallel

ompreduce.title: omp_reduction
ompreduce.name: omp_reduction
ompreduce.summary: Reduction clause for parallel accumulation operations

params.+ (addition): Identity value: 0. Combines partial sums from all threads.
params.- (subtraction): Identity value: 0. Note: Subtraction is not truly associative; treated as addition of negated values.
params.* (multiplication): Identity value: 1. Combines partial products from all threads.
params..and. (logical AND): Identity value: .true.. Result is .true. only if all partial results are .true..
params..or. (logical OR): Identity value: .false.. Result is .true. if any partial result is .true..
params..eqv. (logical equivalence): Identity value: .true.. Tests if all partial results have the same logical value.
params..neqv. (logical non-equivalence): Identity value: .false.. Logical XOR across all threads.
params.max (maximum): Identity value: smallest representable value for the type. Finds maximum across all threads.
params.min (minimum): Identity value: largest representable value for the type. Finds minimum across all threads.
params.iand (bitwise AND): Identity value: all bits set to 1. Performs bitwise AND across all threads.
params.ior (bitwise OR): Identity value: 0. Performs bitwise OR across all threads.
params.ieor (bitwise XOR): Identity value: 0. Performs bitwise XOR across all threads.

ompreduce.description:
**reduction(operator:list)** is a data-sharing clause that enables safe parallel accumulation of values into shared variables. Without reduction, multiple threads updating the same variable would cause a race condition. With reduction, each thread accumulates into its own private copy, and these copies are combined at the end of the parallel region.

 The private copies are initialized to the identity value for the operator: 0 for +, 1 for *, .true. for .and., .false. for .or., largest negative for max, largest positive for min, all bits set for iand, and zero for ior and ieor.
ompreduce.result: After the parallel region completes, the reduction variable contains the combined result of the reduction operation applied across all threads. The order of combination is implementation-defined but mathematically equivalent to sequential execution for associative operators.
ompreduce.example_code:
program demo_omp_reduction
  use omp_lib
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n = 10000
  real(8) :: a(n)
  real(8) :: sum_val, product_val, max_val, min_val
  integer :: count_positive
  logical :: all_positive, any_negative
  integer :: i

  ! Initialize array with mixed values
  do i = 1, n
    a(i) = real(i - n/2, 8)  ! Values from -5000 to 5000
  end do

  ! Reduction with + (sum)
  sum_val = 0.0d0
  !$omp parallel do reduction(+:sum_val)
  do i = 1, n
    sum_val = sum_val + a(i)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,F15.2)', 'Sum:     ', sum_val

  ! Reduction with max
  max_val = -huge(max_val)
  !$omp parallel do reduction(max:max_val)
  do i = 1, n
    max_val = max(max_val, a(i))
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,F15.2)', 'Maximum: ', max_val

  ! Reduction with min
  min_val = huge(min_val)
  !$omp parallel do reduction(min:min_val)
  do i = 1, n
    min_val = min(min_val, a(i))
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,F15.2)', 'Minimum: ', min_val

  ! Logical reduction: .and.
  all_positive = .true.
  !$omp parallel do reduction(.and.:all_positive)
  do i = 1, n
    all_positive = all_positive .and. (a(i) > 0.0d0)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,L)', 'All positive: ', all_positive

  ! Logical reduction: .or.
  any_negative = .false.
  !$omp parallel do reduction(.or.:any_negative)
  do i = 1, n
    any_negative = any_negative .or. (a(i) < 0.0d0)
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,L)', 'Any negative: ', any_negative

  ! Integer reduction: count
  count_positive = 0
  !$omp parallel do reduction(+:count_positive)
  do i = 1, n
    if (a(i) > 0.0d0) count_positive = count_positive + 1
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A,I0)', 'Count positive: ', count_positive

  ! Multiple reductions in one directive
  sum_val = 0.0d0
  max_val = -huge(max_val)
  min_val = huge(min_val)
  !$omp parallel do reduction(+:sum_val) reduction(max:max_val) reduction(min:min_val)
  do i = 1, n
    sum_val = sum_val + a(i)
    max_val = max(max_val, a(i))
    min_val = min(min_val, a(i))
  end do
  !$omp end parallel do
  print '(A)', 'Combined reductions:'
  print '(A,F15.2)', '  Sum: ', sum_val
  print '(A,F15.2)', '  Max: ', max_val
  print '(A,F15.2)', '  Min: ', min_val

end program demo_omp_reduction
